title: Learned metasurface codes produce measured single and paired beams
summary: A physics-assisted ResNet34 produced coding configurations applied to a programmable metasurface. Measurements of four designs showed fields in prescribed single- and dual-beam directions, with unequal beam strength in one case. This is a limited physical design check, without AI credit for a new electromagnetic law or autonomous tracking deployment.

source_review.scope: Original selected computational/clinical or physical Methods, model role, specific Results and limitations read; operational biological sections excluded

evidence.ai_role: The trained inverse network outputs metasurface coding from human-specified beam targets; a conventional electromagnetic forward model supplies the learning loss. Learned coding is separate from the human-designed metasurface and macroscopic physics.
evidence.tested: Four network-generated configurations were measured in an anechoic chamber for forward/slanted single beams and paired beams. Measurements covered only a limited angular region. Additional static target-position examples were shown.
evidence.unknown: The forward model omits mutual coupling; the source reports degraded performance when interactions are included. Continuous network phase outputs approximate a binary physical surface. One dual-beam case showed unequal intensity attributed to specular reflection. Selected tests do not establish arbitrary-beam generalization, independent replication, real closed-loop tracking or a physical mechanism discovered by AI.
